newsitem.title: SPAIN: Morocco seizes Spanish trawlers - shipowner.
newsitem.headline: Morocco seizes Spanish trawlers - shipowner.

text.p: Morocco seized two Spanish trawlers fishing off its coast in an effort to press the European Union to extend a two-month selective fishing ban in the area, one of the shipowners said on Tuesday.
Spanish media reported that on Monday Morocco seized two trawlers, one for allegedly fishing too close to the coast, the other for allegedly fishing without a licence.
The Agriculture Ministry was unable to confirm the seizure and said it was awaiting confirmation from Moroccan authorities.
Shipowner Paulino Estevez denied the boats had been fishing illegally and said the move was a ploy to discredit Spanish trawlers during Morocco's discussions with the EU.
"The navigation apparatus will show that we were not fishing illegally," he told reporters.
Morocco is in talks with the EU to extend a two-month fishing ban on over-exploited cephalopods - which includes octopus, squid and cuttlefish - to give them time to grow.

Morocco was in conflict with Spain over the renewal of its fishing accord last year. After months of wrangling Morocco finally reached a four-year fisheries agreement with the EU under which the EU pays Morocco $162.5 million a year in fees for fishing rights for the mainly Spanish fleet.
The accord allows 600 fishing boats from southern Spain, the Canary islands and Portugal to operate in Moroccan waters.
